db_evidence.notes: The correct battle can be localized via text/SQL search on episode captions -- the boss name banner '快如风' flashes in 30sec captions around 65370-65400, and the victory screen text '已击败 兵刀·急如火·快如风' appears at 65670-65700 -- but this text is buried inside long free-text captions and is not consistently surfaced by the semantic_search/run_sql queries the agents tried (2 of 5 rollouts never found it at all). The literal string 'perfect dodge' / '完美闪避' does not occur anywhere in episodes/visual_clips/semantic_triples text (checked directly via sql), so the count itself is never retrievable from structured/text memory -- it can only be obtained via clip_qa watching the raw video for a brief visual flash/afterimage cue, which is inherently hard to sample correctly at coarse fps and inherently unverifiable against the boss's identity unless the visual sub-agent is explicitly shown the boss name/banner frame first.

root_causes: 2 of 5 rollouts (2, 3, 4) never located the actual battle window (65340-65670s); their text/semantic search for the boss name 'Rapid as Fire and Swift as Wind' failed because the boss-name banner is a fleeting caption fragment inside long free-text episode descriptions rather than a distinct searchable field, and no table stores 'perfect dodge' as literal text.

In the 2 rollouts with wrong localization that still scored 5 (rollout 2 and 4), clip_qa was dispatched to an arbitrary/wrong scene and self-reported finding 'the encounter' without ever cross-checking the boss name/victory banner visually, then produced a count (3) that coincidentally matched the reference -- correct answer for the wrong reason, undetectable by a judge that only compares the final count.

In rollout 0 (correct localization, wrong answer), the visual sub-agent's frame sampling/detection of the 'perfect dodge' flash was imprecise: it found a dodge at a non-clue timestamp (65386.7s) and missed all 3 true clue instants split across window boundaries (65400s and 65520s cut splits sit right next to two of the three real clue intervals at 65407 and 65505/65551), suggesting boundary effects and/or an unreliable visual criterion for what counts as a 'perfect dodge' flash versus an ordinary dodge/attack-impact flash.

Judge apparently scores only the final numeric answer against the reference ('3'), not the supporting evidence or reasoning validity, so two rollouts that hallucinated the wrong battle entirely still scored a perfect 5.
what_worked: Rollout 1 correctly localized the fight via run_sql on episodes filtered to a plausible time band, then split the fight into 3 sequential clip_qa sub-windows covering the whole battle, and its visual sub-agent's per-window dodge counts summed to the right total (3) even though individual timestamps were only approximately right.

Splitting a long battle into multiple bounded clip_qa windows (rather than one long window) was used by both rollout 0 and rollout 1 and let the visual agent focus on shorter, more tractable segments.
transferable_lessons: For 'named battle' questions, first confirm you have the right encounter by finding a title/banner/victory-screen text match (e.g. the boss name appearing in a caption) before sending clip_qa anywhere -- do not let clip_qa self-select 'the encounter that seems to match' from an arbitrary time window.

When a count of a purely visual, non-textual event (e.g. an on-screen effect flash) is asked, expect zero hits from semantic_search/run_sql on 'perfect dodge' style text and go straight to localizing the scene by other means (boss name, entities, event_chains) before relying on clip_qa's raw counting.
When splitting a battle into consecutive clip_qa windows, add small overlaps at window boundaries so a dodge event straddling a cut isn't missed or double-handled by neither/both adjacent calls.

A clip_qa call that returns 'I found the encounter here' should be treated skeptically unless it also confirms an identifying detail (boss name/banner) visible on screen; otherwise it may be answering about the wrong fight while still returning a plausible-looking count.
open_questions: What exact visual cue constitutes a 'perfect dodge' in this game (a UI text popup, a specific color flash, a slow-motion trigger) was never directly confirmed by inspecting the true clue-interval frames at high fps; a single frame at 65408s showed no obvious on-screen dodge indicator, so the cue is likely a very brief (sub-second) effect that requires denser frame sampling than most rollouts used.
Whether the judge for this question type ever checks timestamp/evidence plausibility in addition to the final count, given that 2 rollouts with a completely wrong battle location still scored 5.
